speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are presenting with frequent epistaxis, bleeding from mucous membranes, and petechiae. To understand the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any other bruising on your body or any recent injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given the history of gum bleeding and unexplained bruising alongside the nosebleeds and petechiae, have you noticed any family members with similar bleeding problems or a history of easy bruising? REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Count

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The clinical presentation of mucous membrane bleeding, petechiae, and diffuse bruising in a 4-year-old male without a family history is highly characteristic of ITP.
